title: Interview scratchpad — Runtime Lead (Elysia Cho)
content:
Quick context / primer:
- Role: Runtime Lead (team: serving runtime). Hiring bar: strong systems + people manager, shipping low-latency inference features, cross-team execution.
- Candidate: Elysia Cho — ex-infra at a mid-stage ML infra startup, previously systems lead at CloudOps Co. Strong resume: shipping model-serving at scale, ops and CI experience, some open-source contributions to quantization tooling.

High-level impressions (first pass):
- Comfortable talking systems-level tradeoffs; explained KV cache invalidation and dedupe strategies clearly.
- Strong ownership examples — drove a cross-functional rollout for a low-latency feature (retries + circuit breaker) at previous company.
- Communication: concise, pragmatic. Not overly abstract. Good at defining metrics.

Technical deep-dive notes (interviewers' bullets):
- Sequence cache design: candidate proposed prefix-based shard keys and time-to-live eviction plus LRU fallback. Asked about multi-tenant isolation and proposed simple tenant-aware cache namespace. Pros: simple; Cons: needs memory accounting. I noted she didn't call out per-tenant memory hard-limits — follow up.
- Quantization/precision: solid conceptual understanding. Has experience with int8 paths on Turing GPUs; described empirical calibration step. Asked about kernel selection — mentioned ability to work with compiler team, not a kernel hacker herself.
- Latency SLO handling: suggested degrading to smaller context length + offload KV warming during low-traffic windows. Practical and measurable.
- CI / rollout: described canarying + automatic rollback on p90 regression. Implementation details light — would rely on SRE/Platform for infra pieces.

Coding exercise (live pair):
- Prompt: implement simplified concurrent request coalescing + cache lookup.
- Outcome: delivered working sketch, used Go-style channels in pseudocode (candidate prefers Go). Code had edge-case handling for races, but missed one race when cache entry is deleted concurrently — pointed out during post-hoc discussion.
- Speed: moderate; correctness-first. Suggests hands-on but not rapid-fire algorithmist.

Leadership / org fit notes:
- Management style: mentors ICs, prefers 1:1s focused on career plans. Seems to bias toward hiring senior ICs and delegating implementation.
- Cross-team: has run cross-functional projects involving product, infra, and data science. Good at translating product SLAs into infra stories.
- Hiring: asked about leveling and scorecards; concrete process suggestions (rubrics, paired hiring interviews).

Scorecard (my draft numeric scales 1-5, leave for calibration):
- System design: 4
- Low-level performance optimization: 3
- Operational experience (rollouts/SLOs): 4
- Coding + correctness: 3
- Leadership & cross-team ops: 4
- Communication: 4
- Overall hire recommendation: strong hire for engineer-manager track, hire if looking for lead engineer with PM-lite responsibilities.

Concerns / open questions (to resolve before final):
- Kernel-level expertise: not a device/kernel expert. If we need someone to implement fast kernels or deep CUDA work, this may be a gap. For coordinating with compiler/kernel teams she's fine.
- Memory accounting & multi-tenant limits: didn't propose hard resource enforcement; follow-up question: how would she set admission control thresholds?
- On-call stamina: limited direct on-call history at scale (she's done ops but small team). Need SRE to support ramp.

Action items / next steps (TODOs):
- Samir to ask follow-up on admission control and per-tenant memory limits (email thread).
- Jenna to run short behavioral check focused on conflict resolution with product (15m).
- If positive, schedule hiring manager debrief (Priya + Eng Dir) with calibrated scorecards.

Suggested interview priorities for next round:
- Deep dive on admission control: concrete algorithms and metrics (how to cap per-tenant KV cache, eviction heuristics under overload).
- Cross-team execution example with measurable outcomes (timeline, metrics improved).
- Small whiteboard kernel selection question: given three candidate kernels with tradeoffs (latency vs. memory vs. p95 variance), ask to pick and justify with instrumentation plan.

Red flags observed (low-impact but note):
- Slight tendency to assume ops will be available to fill gaps; will need to probe autonomy and ownership boundaries.
- Preference for hiring senior engineers could slow headcount ramp for a scaling team; want to check hiring velocity approach.

Random notes / quotes I liked:
- "I measure a rollout's success by whether you can remove the feature without customer impact — not by if rollout succeeded." (good practical framing)
- Brought up a subtle point about warming KV caches during predicted traffic surges rather than on-the-fly cold starts — practical cost/latency tradeoff.

Recommendation (draft):
- Move to hiring manager + culture debrief. Strong candidate for the Lead/Manager role depending on comp and expectations. Not the right hire if the top priority is deep CUDA/kernel work.

Files to attach in full packet (if we progress):
- Candidate resume (PDF)
- Pairing session recording + code snippet (Samir to upload)
- List of reference questions for 2 refs (Jenna to draft)

Notes to self: keep scorecard numeric fields aligned with other interviews before sending to Dir. Add a short one-paragraph summary for recruiter to forward to candidate with timeline.

End of scratchpad.
